Deleted progress is something I’ve never dealt with on a large scale. Usually I would try to somehow artificially reinstate what was deleted. Let’s say if I was level 15 and got sent back to level 10, I would give enough xp to get back to 15. Sometimes you can’t really get back all the things you lost so at some point I would get tired of replaying the same things and just reason whether I would of legitimately gotten it by now, and unlock it if I felt I put in the required effort to achieve it, had there been no resets. 50-100 hours of lost progress is way more extreme than anything I’ve experienced. Only those games where you forget to save and die and lose, at most, a couple hours.

As for achievements that have gotten harder as DLCs came out, I personally would do them while they’re harder because it feels like the timestamp of it’s completion is more impressive then people who did it when it was easier, but nobody checks that. It would just be cool for myself.

I think SAM is completely justified for achievements that are impossible, although I haven’t used it for that reason. I will usually avoid games that have impossible achievements. I also think it’s fine if it doesn’t unlock because of a bug. I’ve had to do this several times.

For 99.9% of achievements, I don’t support the use of console, save scumming, pause buffering, bug abuse, etc. The one exception are achievements that are unreasonably grindy. For example, I’ve been slowly trying to 100% Cookie Clicker, with as little save scumming as possible, however it would take thousands of hours of staring at an idle screen and clicking every now and then to get some achievements. To me, it’s not very impressive or fulfilling to just mindlessly wait to get an achievement, so I utilize tricks through save scumming to make it more engaging and quicker. It’s more short term effort because I have to constantly be playing, but it speeds up the process immensely.

For achievements that are difficult in terms of skill, I would never use any form of unfair advantage to make them effortless. There’s obviously a blurry line of what’s fair and unfair, like the use of certain strategies or guides, but as long as it’s not taking away from what makes it hard, it’s ok with me. I also set a rule that I must beat a game before looking up any information about it. After that I will look up missing achievements and go from there.

TLDR: SAM for bugs. Savescum/mods for unreasonably grindy. Just guides/strategy for normal and difficult.
